subject: Horizon Health - Hosted API: data residency and retention clarifications
messages:
From: Laura Mitchell <l.mitchell@horizonhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API - Residency/Retention Qs (Horizon Health)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. We're finalizing our vendor security review and have a short set of follow-ups specific to the hosted API: data residency options, retention windows, deletion guarantees, and backup handling. I've attached our questionnaire (Horizon_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx).

High level asks:
- Can you confirm where customer input (prompts + files) is stored and whether customers can restrict hosting to a specific region?
- What is your default retention period for request logs and generated outputs?
- If we request deletion for a tenant, what is the end-to-end timeline (including backups/snapshots)?

We're on a tight procurement cadence and would appreciate a brief summary by EOD Monday so we can move to contract review. Happy to hop on a short call if useful.

Thanks,
Laura Mitchell
Vendor Security, Horizon Health
[attachment: Horizon_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Mitchell <l.mitchell@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - Residency/Retention Qs (Horizon Health)

Hi Laura — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. I've drafted answers below and attached a doc with proposed responses for your questionnaire. Ben and Grace are cc'd for technical/security validation; Ben can confirm the routing/region details and Grace can confirm deletion and backup flows.

Draft summary (high level):
- Residency: Redwood's hosted API defaults to US regions (us-east-1) for new accounts. We offer region pinning to EU regions (eu-west-1) for customers with EU data residency requirements; please request during provisioning and we will enable the tenant in the requested region.
- Retention: By default, request logs and generated outputs are retained for 30 days. Customers on an enterprise contract can select shorter retention (7 days) or opt into retention-free mode for ephemeral prompt-only usage; we document tradeoffs for diagnostics and rate-limiting.
- Deletion: Customer-initiated deletion requests start a workflow that purges tenant data from the active serving layer within 48 hours; backups and long-term snapshots are scheduled for removal on the next snapshot cycle (typically within 30 days). We provide written confirmation when deletion is complete.

I attached the current draft (redwood_horizon_data_answers_v1.docx) — please let me know any edits and whether you want a more formal attestation or a short call.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Strategic Account Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_horizon_data_answers_v1.docx]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - Residency/Retention Qs (Horizon Health)

Vanessa — quick tech notes on the draft:

- Residency nuance: default tenant placement is us-east-1, but we can provision in us-west-2 or eu-west-1 depending on contract. For corporate customers requiring strict EU-only processing, we recommend private deployment (Redwood Private) or dedicated capacity in eu-west-1; for most customers we do region pinning in hosted API and ensure inference + storage remain in-region.
- Data classification: prompts + files are treated as customer-supplied content and stored encrypted at rest. Metadata we retain for routing/observability (e.g., model, token counts) can be configured to a minimal set if Horizon requests reduced telemetry.
- Deletion detail: purge from live volumes <48 hours after request; snapshots are immutable in the short term — we run weekly snapshot roll and a retention policy that expires snapshots after 30 days by default. If Horizon requires accelerated snapshot purge as a contractual point, we can add a 14-day snapshot expiry for the account.

I'll flag one wording item in the doc: avoid saying "permanent deletion instantly" — we should be explicit about snapshots and backups. Happy to review the updated wording.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - Residency/Retention Qs (Horizon Health)

Adding security controls and compliance language for the questionnaire:

- Encryption: All customer data (in-flight and at rest) is encrypted with TLS 1.3 and AES-256. Keys are managed via customer-isolated KMS instances for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS with strict access control and rotation policies.
- Access & audit logs: Tenant-level access is logged; audit logs are retained for 90 days by default and can be extended per contract. Logs include token usage, API keys used, and admin console actions.
- Deletion attestation: We provide a deletion certificate (signed document) when a full tenant purge is completed. The certificate includes timestamps for active-store purge and expected snapshot expiry.
- Backups & snapshots: Backups are encrypted and retained on separate storage with strict lifecycle rules. For hosted API customers, the standard GCP/AWS snapshot retention is 30 days. For customers requiring shorter retention we can set a 14-day snapshot expiry and document in the SLA.
- SOC 2 reference: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II audited; see summary attached. For a full report we execute an NDA and SSO flow as required.

Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf

Grace O'Connor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
[attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf]

Subject: Re: Hosted API - Residency/Retention Qs (Horizon Health)

Hi Laura — thanks for the patience. Below is our consolidated response; I've attached the completed questionnaire and a short attestation doc. If you need any changes to retention windows or snapshot expiry, we can add those to the contract (SOW/SLA).

Consolidated answers (summary):
- Where data is stored: By default, hosted API customer data (prompts, attachments, and generated outputs) is stored in the customer's tenant region (us-east-1) for U.S. accounts. We offer region pinning to eu-west-1 upon request; private/dedicated deployments are available for strict regional isolation.

- Default retention windows: Active request logs and outputs: 30 days. Audit logs (access/admin): 90 days. Enterprise options: 7-day or retention-free ephemeral mode for request data; extended audit log retention available on contract.

- Deletion workflow & timeline:
  * Customer requests deletion via support or the admin console.
  * Active data purge from serving volumes: completed within 48 hours.
  * Snapshot/backup expiry: standard hosted snapshot expiry is 30 days; we can contractually agree to 14-day expiry for Horizon.
  * Deletion attestation: Redwood issues a signed deletion certificate when the active purge is complete and provides confirmation when snapshots reach expiry.

- Backups & compliance: Backups are encrypted and managed with lifecycle policies. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II audited; we can provide the full report under NDA.

Next steps: I've uploaded the completed questionnaire and a short attestation to a shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example-redwood-horizon-answer-set. I can also provide a one-page contract clause for a 14-day snapshot expiry if Horizon prefers that added to the SOW.

Would you like me to loop in procurement/legal to draft the clause, or should we wait until Horizon signs off on the answers?

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Strategic Account Manager, Redwood Inference
